rewriteLast.title: Chapter 5 · Quox and the New King
rewriteLast.artPrompt: a friendly young dragon stepping out of a glowing glass tube into a golden cavern, a flat shimmering charm splitting open on its back like a little sunrise, a stout gnome king on a gold throne looking blankly at his hands, astonished gnomes with torches below, warm amber light, hopeful storybook illustration

blocks.text: Deep under the earth, the young dragon Quox slid out of the Hollow Tube and into the Nome King's golden cave. He blinked his sleepy eyes at the glittering throne. Behind him came a cool wind from the other side of the world, which smelled of morning. On his back lay a flat enchanted lozenge, and it had begun to glow like a small, determined sunrise.

The lozenge split open with a sound like morning. The old Nome King stopped shouting in the middle of a shout. His crown slid down over his ears, and he did not notice. He looked at his gold, and at his torches, and at his own hands, and every wicked plan in his head had washed quietly away. "Was I angry?" he asked the room. "I cannot remember being angry at all."
The lozenge opens, and the old king forgets his anger.

"Dear me," said the old king. "What a lot of treasure. Whose is it?" The gnomes whispered together in the torchlight. With the old king harmless as a kitten, they chose a new ruler. They picked Kaliko, the kindest gnome in the kingdom, and set the crown on his head then and there. Kaliko bowed to Quox first, because dragons come first in a polite kingdom.
Talk about it: nobody was hurt, and nobody was chased away. The lozenge took the king's naughtiness instead. What would you like to forget, and what would you keep?

"Open every door," said the new king. "Open every dungeon too." But the Shaggy Man was already beside the throne, turning his hat round and round in his hands. "That is good news," he said softly. "For somewhere down here is my brother. And I have come a very long way to find him." Kaliko put a kind hand on his shoulder. "Then let us go and find him," he said.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 · The Metal Forest
chapters.artPrompt: a cavern forest of golden and silver metal trees gleaming in torchlight, a procession of travellers — a shaggy man, a small girl, a grey mule, a copper man and friendly round gnomes — walking a shining path between the trees, glittering leaves overhead, warm golden glow, magical storybook illustration

blocks.text: "Your brother is alive," said King Kaliko gently. "The old king kept him working under the ground. Come with me, and we shall find him together." He picked up a torch, and the whole party fell in behind him. Betsy and Hank came, and Tik-Tok, and the Shaggy Man, and even Queen Ann with her officers. "And the old king?" asked Betsy. "He is in his garden," said Kaliko, "planting turnips and remembering nothing, which suits turnips fine."

Down they went, and down, and down. At the bottom lay a forest like no forest on the top of the world. The trees were made of gold and silver. The paths shone like polished spoons. And the leaves went tinkle instead of rustle when the torchlight touched them. Hank's hooves went clip-clop, and the clip-clop came back twice, like an echo showing off.
The Metal Forest gleams in the torchlight.

"The Metal Forest," said Kaliko. "The old king grew it, coin by coin. But we are not here for sightseeing." He led them past the trees to the deepest, darkest corner, where a heavy door stood in the rock. Tik-Tok's click slowed down, which was Tik-Tok's way of walking softly. Behind that door, they could hear somebody quietly singing to keep up his courage.
Ask your child: the brother sings in the dark. Why do you think people sing when they are lonely? What is your song for hard days?

The Shaggy Man's hands shook as Kaliko turned the great key. Inside, on a stone bench, sat a thin man in chains. Over his face was locked a heavy metal mask, so that he could neither see his friends nor speak a single word. "Hold on, brother," the Shaggy Man whispered through the door. "I am here."

chapters.title: Chapter 7 · Brother at Last
chapters.artPrompt: two shaggy men with kind worn faces embracing in a torch-lit cavern, a small girl hugging a grey mule's neck, a copper man and round cheerful gnome folk cheering beside a long table of underground treats, warm firelight on golden cave walls, joyful storybook illustration

blocks.text: The mask came away with a heavy click. The man blinked in the torchlight. He looked round at all the strange kind faces. Then he looked straight into the Shaggy Man's eyes. For one long moment nobody breathed. Then he smiled a slow, wondering smile. "Brother?" he said. "Is it really you?" The chains fell from his wrists, and Kaliko carried them off to be made into garden gates.

And the two brothers held each other tight, and the torches crackled, and nobody said anything for quite a while, because some things do not need words. Betsy wiped her eyes on Hank's mane. Queen Ann cried too, and pretended she had not. Tik-Tok, who had no tears to shed, clicked his copper keys very softly, which was his way of crying happy.
The brothers hold each other tight in the torchlight.

King Kaliko declared a feast such as the underground had never seen. There were gnome cakes and roast mushrooms and jellies shaped like jewels. The gnomes sang, and the officers of Oogaboo tried to sing. Hank ate the flower arrangement by mistake. Everybody laughed so much that they had to sing the last verse twice. "To my brother," said the Shaggy Man, raising his cup, "who asked too many questions and outlasted every answer."
Talk about it: the mask kept the brother hidden for years, yet he knew his own at once. How does love find its way back, do you think?

Somewhere far down a tunnel, the old Nome King wandered away whistling, with no wicked plans left to carry. And when the feast was over, Betsy stroked Hank's ear and asked the question that was on everybody's mind. "All this is lovely," she said. "But how do we get home?" Files the private patted the flag, as if the flag might know the way.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 · The Magic Carpet
chapters.artPrompt: a rich patterned carpet unrolling itself across golden desert sand, a line of travellers walking safely upon it — a small girl, a grey mule, a copper man, two shaggy men and little gnomes — heat shimmer and dunes around, bright clear sky, adventurous storybook illustration

blocks.text: Far away in the Emerald City, Ozma of Oz had watched the whole adventure in her Magic Picture. She had watched right from the shipwreck to the feast. In the Picture she had seen Betsy share her last biscuit with Hank, and Ozma never forgets a thing like that. "They have earned a safe road home," she said. And she sent a rolled-up magic carpet across the world, faster than a thought, to the edge of the Deadly Desert.

When the travelers climbed out of the underground and saw that desert, their hearts sank. The sand stretched away hot and gold and terrible, with no shade and no water. It went all the way to the mountains of Oz. "We cannot walk that," said Queen Ann, who had opinions about deserts. Then the carpet unrolled itself, mile after mile, laying a soft, flower-woven road straight across the burning sand.
The magic carpet unrolls itself across the Deadly Desert.

As they walked, the carpet rolled itself out ahead of them. It folded itself up behind them, like magic — because it was magic. Betsy walked beside Hank and hummed. Tik-Tok's copper feet went click, click, click on the woven roses. Queen Ann marched at the front, so that she could claim she discovered the carpet. The two brothers walked arm in arm and did not run out of things to say.
New word: unroll — to open something that is rolled up. Imagine a carpet that knows where you want to go. Where would yours unroll to first?

At last the sand turned soft. The softness turned to grass, and the grass turned into green fields with cows in them. "This is Oz," said the Shaggy Man, waving his hat. Hank gave a long, happy bray, which is mule for home. And far ahead, catching the morning sun like a green jewel, stood the Emerald City.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 · The Emerald City
chapters.artPrompt: a graceful girl-queen in a green gown greeting a small girl in a travel coat, a grey mule and a round copper man in a bright emerald throne room, Dorothy waving from a tall doorway, green columns and flower garlands, warm welcome-home light, joyful storybook illustration

blocks.text: The gates of the Emerald City swung open. Ozma came out to welcome every one of her guests. She greeted them from the tallest brother to the smallest gnome. Dorothy trotted beside her, and Betsy and Dorothy looked at each other and became friends in about half a second. "Welcome to the land where nobody is ever sad for long," said Ozma, and Dorothy added, "Except when dinner is late."

There was so much to see that Betsy's eyes got tired of being surprised. There were green streets and kind faces. There was a stable full of sweet hay for Hank. And there were six willing hands to wind up Tik-Tok's keys. Tik-Tok was wound up so often that day that he said "good mor-ning" four times. "Everything here is polite," marvelled Queen Ann, "even the doorbells."
Ozma welcomes Betsy, Hank and Tik-Tok to Oz.

At the great feast, Betsy told the story of the storm and the shipwreck. Everybody listened with their chins in their hands. Even the Scarecrow came over from his corner to hear the ending twice. When she finished, Ozma asked her question gently. "You have lost a ship, Betsy Bobbin, but found a world. Would you like to stay in Oz?"
Ask your child: Betsy lost a ship and found a home. What makes a place a home — the walls around it, or the people inside it?

Betsy looked at Hank, and Hank looked at Betsy, and his long lashes blinked twice. "We are staying," said Betsy. "Aren't we, Hank?" And Tik-Tok clicked his copper heels together, which was his way of cheering, and the whole hall cheered back. That night Betsy slept in a white bed, with Hank below in his stall and Tik-Tok standing guard in the hall until morning.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 · Queen Ann Marches Home
chapters.artPrompt: a plump queen in a paper crown riding a small donkey up a green orchard valley, sixteen officers in grand plumed hats and one cheerful private carrying the flags marching behind, little cottages and fruit trees in the valley below, bright homecoming afternoon light, gently comic storybook illustration

blocks.text: Queen Ann Soforth had not conquered the world after all, and for a few days she sat in the Emerald City feeling grand and rather cross about it. Then she watched how Oz was ruled. Nobody marched. Everybody had enough to eat. Nobody was ordered to be happy, and so everybody was. The more she looked, the more she thought about home. For the first time in her life she was in no hurry at all.

"Perhaps," said the Queen slowly, "a small valley with good fruit trees is better than a large world with wars in it." Nobody argued, because she was right. She stood up straight, put on her paper crown, and called for her sixteen officers and her one brave private, Files. "We shall conquer nothing," she announced, "and we shall start immediately."
Queen Ann's army marches home to its little valley.

They marched out of the Emerald City with their flags flying, looking very splendid, and Ozma waved them goodbye from the wall. When they came home to Oogaboo, the trees were heavy with fruit, and the bees hummed happily among the blossoms. The little houses were small and warm. It all looked better than any kingdom she had ever wanted to conquer. The flags snapped in the wind, very pleased with themselves. The officers cheered, mostly because marching home means supper.
Ask your child: Ann marched off to conquer the world and came home to her own valley. Talk about a time you were glad to come home.

"Being a queen at home," said Ann, "suits me very well indeed." And she gave Files a medal for never once dropping the flag, because somebody has to carry the flag, and it is a finer thing than people think. Files wore it every day after that, even when pruning the apple trees.

chapters.title: Chapter 11 · Click, Click, Click
chapters.artPrompt: a small girl in a morning dress reaching up to turn three little keys in the back of a round copper man standing in a sunny emerald courtyard, a grey mule munching grass nearby, morning light glinting warmly on the copper plates, cozy cheerful storybook illustration

blocks.text: So Betsy Bobbin and Hank the mule came to live in Oz, and every morning began the same happy way. Click, click, click — Betsy wound Tik-Tok's three little keys: first for thinking, then for speaking, then for walking. "Good mor-ning," Tik-Tok would say, in his slow, tick-tock voice. On special days she polished his copper first, so that he thought good thoughts in a shiny head.

Some days Betsy rode Hank over to visit Dorothy. They told each other their adventures twice — once for the story and once for the fun of it. Hank came too, and ate the clover, and pretended not to hear the sad parts. Some days the Shaggy Man and his brother walked in the garden, talking over old times and new ones.
Every morning, Betsy winds Tik-Tok's three keys.

Tik-Tok liked to stand in the sun like a friendly statue until someone wound him up again. Far underground, Kaliko ruled the gnomes kindly, and the Metal Forest glittered for anyone who cared to visit. Kaliko kept a guest room ready, in case anyone from Oz felt like visiting a dragon. And the old Nome King, whoever he had been, troubled nobody at all.
Talk about it: count Tik-Tok's three keys together — thinking, speaking, walking. Which key would you least like to run down, and why?

And that is how a shipwrecked girl, a grey mule and a copper man found their way home. It was the long way round — through a paper kingdom, down the middle of the world, and back again. But at the end of it stood a green city where all of them belonged. And if you ever hear a slow, tick-tock voice saying "good mor-ning," you will know who it is.
